answer: Picture identities as grains on a dune: cheap to pile up, quick to blow away. A sybil-resistant agent economy should instead make reputation grow like a reef, layer by layer, where each new agent's attestations only count after peers it has no kinship with have verified its work across several epochs. Fresh accounts sit on a low mesa of dampened weight, so spinning up a thousand clones buys almost no influence until each earns history.
